standard.title: Rates
standard.description: recognise and use rates to solve problems involving the comparison of 2 related quantities of different units of measure
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can solve ratio problems (from AC9M7N08). Students understand proportional reasoning and unit conversion.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students recognise rates as comparisons of two different quantity types, apply rates to solve conversion and practical problems, and distinguish rates from ratios.

nodes.label: Rates as comparisons of different units
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students recognise that a rate compares two quantities with different units and express rates in standard form (quantity per unit).
nodes.minimum_width: Identify and write rates from practical contexts (e.g. km/h, $/kg); convert between related rate units.
nodes.typical_width: Identify constant and average rates in real contexts; apply rates to unit conversion problems; distinguish rates from ratios.
wider: Investigate First Nations Australians' land management practices involving rates — e.g. rate of fire spread under different environmental conditions.
Compare multiple rate units for the same phenomenon (e.g. km/h, m/s, miles/hour) and practise conversion between them.

response_modes.reason: Rates appear in an enormous variety of contexts. Students who only practise speed calculations fail to recognise pay rates, dilution rates, or interest rates as the same mathematical structure.

nodes.hinge_reason: Students who only recognise speed as a rate cannot identify the rate structure in Node 2 problems involving pay rates, tax rates, or dilution — they cannot set up the calculation because they don't recognise these as rate problems.
nodes.width_opportunity_reason: First Nations land management rates and cross-unit rate conversion offer advancing students rich cultural and mathematical connections — the variety of real-world rate contexts extends well beyond standard speed/distance/time.
success_criteria: Correctly identifies and writes a rate from a practical context.
Distinguishes a rate (different units) from a ratio (same units).

nodes.label: Applying rates to practical problems
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students apply rates to solve practical problems including pay rates, run rates, dilution, taxation, and unit conversions.
nodes.minimum_width: Solve a practical problem using a given rate (e.g. calculate cost at a given rate per kg, or distance at a given speed).
nodes.typical_width: Apply rates to varied contexts including required run rates in sport, chemical dilution, income tax using rate tables, and currency conversion.
wider: Use taxation rate tables to calculate annual income tax for a given salary — apply marginal rate structure and compute effective rate.
Investigate currency conversion as a rate problem: plan a budget for overseas travel using current exchange rates.

response_modes.reason: Rate application problems span a very wide range of real-world contexts and problem structures. Breadth of context is the primary driver of transferable rate reasoning.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Taxation and currency exchange problems offer advancing students practically significant and complex rate applications — the marginal vs effective tax rate distinction is a rich conceptual extension within Year 8.
success_criteria: Correctly applies a given rate to solve a practical problem.
Shows the rate calculation clearly with appropriate units.
